question: What do they mean by global and local context?

evidence: In contrast, in order to exploit section information, in this paper we propose to capture a distributed representation of both the global (the whole document) and the local context (e.g., the section/topic) when deciding if a sentence should be included in the summary

extractive_spans: global (the whole document) and the local context (e.g., the section/topic)
evidence: In contrast, in order to exploit section information, in this paper we propose to capture a distributed representation of both the global (the whole document) and the local context (e.g., the section/topic) when deciding if a sentence should be included in the summary

title: Extractive Summarization of Long Documents by Combining Global and Local Context
answer_short: local context: the topic/section; global context: the whole document
answer_rationale: Text 4 and Text 6 define local context as the topic/section and global context as the whole document. Text 10 also supports this by stating the model incorporates both local and global context information, motivated by the natural topic-oriented structure of long documents.
